The characters in the American animated television series ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants]]'' were created by artist, animator, and former [[marine biologist]] [[Stephen Hillenburg]]. The series chronicles the adventures of the character [[SpongeBob SquarePants (character)|SpongeBob SquarePants]] and his various friends in the fictional underwater city of Bikini Bottom. Most characters are anthropomorphic sea creatures based on real-life species. Many of the characters' designs originated in an educational comic book titled ''The Intertidal Zone'', which Hillenburg created in the 1980s. 

''SpongeBob SquarePants'' features the voices of [[Tom Kenny]], [[Bill Fagerbakke]], [[Rodger Bumpass]], [[Clancy Brown]], [[Mr. Lawrence]], [[Jill Talley]], [[Carolyn Lawrence]], [[Mary Jo Catlett]] and [[Lori Alan]]. Most of the secondary, one-off and background characters are voiced by [[Dee Bradley Baker]], [[Sirena Irwin]], [[Bob Joles]], [[Mark Fite]] and [[Thomas F. Wilson]]. In addition to the series' regular cast, various celebrities from a wide range of professions have voiced guest characters and recurring roles.

The show's characters have received positive critical reception and attention from celebrities. They have made frequent appearances in media outside of the television show, including a [[SpongeBob SquarePants (film series)|theatrical film series]], many [[SpongeBob SquarePants video games|video games]], and two spin-off series. The characters have also been referenced and parodied throughout popular culture. The character SpongeBob became a merchandising icon during the height of the show's second season and has seen continued commercial popularity.

==Creation and conception==
Stephen Hillenburg originally conceived early versions of the ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' characters in 1984, while he was teaching and studying [[marine biology]] at what is now the [[Ocean Institute|Orange County Marine Institute]] in [[Dana Point, California]].<ref name="Banks, pp. 8-9" /> During this period, Hillenburg became fascinated with animation, and wrote a [[comic book]] titled ''The Intertidal Zone'' starring various [[anthropomorphic]] forms of sea creatures, many of which would evolve into ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' characters,<ref name="Banks, p. 9" /> including "Bob the Sponge", who was the co-host of the comic and resembled an actual [[sea sponge]] as opposed to SpongeBob.<ref name="Hillenburg" /> In 1987, Hillenburg left the institute to pursue his dream of becoming an animator.<ref name="Banks, p. 9"/><ref name="Hillenburg" />

[[File:Early sketches of SpongeBob SquarePants main characters.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An early drawing of the initial main characters from Hillenburg's [[bible (screenwriting)|series bible]]]]
Patrick, Mr. Krabs, Pearl, and Squidward were the first other characters Hillenburg created for the show.<ref name="BoytoBob">{{cite magazine|title=From Boy to Bob|magazine=[[Nickelodeon Magazine|Nick Mag Presents: SpongeBob SquarePants]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|date=June 2003}}</ref> Many of their characteristics were based on Hillenburg's experiences during his time at the Ocean Institute or inspired by the traits of their species. Patrick's personality embodies the nature of the starfish; according to Hillenburg, they look "dumb and slow" but are "very active and aggressive" in reality, like Patrick.<ref name="Case">Hillenburg, Stephen. (March 1, 2003). ''The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie'' (''The Case of the Sponge "Bob"'') (DVD). Paramount Home Entertainment/Nickelodeon.</ref> Hillenburg drew inspiration from his former manager at a seafood restaurant while creating Mr. Krabs.<ref name="minipage">{{cite web|url=http://nieonline.com/coloradonie/downloads/minipage/minipage7.15.15.pdf|title=What a Sponge!|work=[[The Mini Page]]|publisher=[[Andrews McMeel Universal]]|date=July 12, 2015}}</ref> According to him, this manager was redheaded, muscular, and a former army cook; these traits were all adapted into Krabs' character.<ref name="Beck84"/> His decision to design Pearl was influenced by his regular supervision of [[whale watching|whale watch]]es at the Ocean Institute, as well as by a cetacean skeleton at the institute.<ref name="neuwirth">{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/makintoonsinside0000neuw/page/50 |title=Makin' Toons: Inside the Most Popular Animated TV Shows and Movies |publisher=[[Skyhorse Publishing]] |last=Neuwirth |first=Allan |date=April 1, 2003 |page=[https://archive.org/details/makintoonsinside0000neuw/page/50 50] |isbn=978-1581152692 |author-link=Allan Neuwirth }}</ref> He drew Pearl with an oversized, almost geometric head as a reference to sperm whales having the largest brain size of any extant animal on Earth.<ref name="BoytoBob"/> He designed Squidward as an octopus because of the species' bulbous mantle; the octopus, he said, has "such a large bulbous head and Squidward thinks he's an intellectual, so of course he's gonna have [one]".<ref name="Case" /> Hillenburg drew Squidward with six tentacles because "it was really just simpler for animation to draw him with six legs instead of eight".<ref name="Case"/>

Several additions were made to the series' main cast before and after Hillenburg pitched the series to [[Nickelodeon]]; in his [[bible (screenwriting)|series bible]], he added Sandy Cheeks, a squirrel clad in a diving suit, as a new friend of SpongeBob.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2014/05/spongebob-squarepants-retrospective-essay|title=How "SpongeBob Squarepants" Stayed Fresh and Subversive Over 15 Years|magazine=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|publisher=[[Verizon Hearst Media Partners]]|last=Encalada|first=Debbie|date=May 1, 2014}}</ref> Plankton and Karen were included in his bible but were not meant to make regular appearances; Plankton's voice actor Mr. Lawrence said that he "was only supposed to be in one or two episodes, but I was a writer on the show and I really liked this character".<ref name="courier">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/138093814/|title=Meet the voice behind a 'SpongeBob' character|newspaper=[[Courier News]]|publisher=[[Gannett Company]]|last=Bourbeau|first=Mary Ann|date=November 15, 2015}}</ref> Following his first voice recording, Lawrence drafted some of his own ideas, hoping to "prove Plankton could survive as more than a one-note character".<ref name="Beck105"/> From then on, Plankton and Karen's roles in the series grew as Lawrence wrote ideas to give them more personality; notably, he decided to write Karen as Plankton's wife, rather than just his computer as was originally intended.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/spongebobsquarep00fain/page/13|title=''SpongeBob SquarePants'' Trivia Book|publisher=[[Simon & Schuster]]|last=Fain|first=David|date=September 1, 2000|page=[https://archive.org/details/spongebobsquarep00fain/page/13 13]|isbn=978-0-689-84018-0}}</ref> They were both officially promoted to main cast members in the credits of the [[The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie|2004 theatrical film]], in which they play central roles.

Hillenburg added Mrs. Puff in response to a request by Nickelodeon that SpongeBob attend school.<ref name="Big Pop Fun">{{cite interview |last=Hillenburg |first=Stephen |subject-link=Stephen Hillenburg |interviewer=[[Thomas F. Wilson]] |title=Big Pop Fun #28: Stephen Hillenburg, Artist and Animator |medium=Podcast |url=https://archive.nerdist.com/big-pop-fun-28-stephen-hillenburg-artist-and-animator/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260227040505/https://archive.nerdist.com/big-pop-fun-28-stephen-hillenburg-artist-and-animator/ |archive-date=February 27, 2026 |format=mp3 |work=[[Nerdist Industries]] |date=May 25, 2012 |access-date=April 10, 2026}}</ref> Initially, Nickelodeon executives felt that children would not relate to SpongeBob because he was an adult.<ref name="Big Pop Fun"/> They told Hillenburg to make SpongeBob more childlike by making him attend school, with a schoolteacher as his authority figure.<ref name="timemagazine">{{Cite magazine |last1=Sands |first1 =Rich |last2=Murphy |first2=Emma |last3=Nashawaty |first3=Chris |last4=Canfield |first4=David |last5=Rigaud |first5=Debbie |last6=Intreglia |first6=Courtney Mifsud |last7=Daspin |first7=Eileen |last8=Hogan |first8=Kate |last9=C |first9=Paris |last10=Greenspan |first10=Rachel E. |last11=Colman |first11=David |url=http://archive.org/details/time-sponge-bob-square-pants-the-global-icon-2025 |title=TIME Special Edition - SpongeBob SquarePants: The Global Icon |date=2025 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|isbn=978-1-5478-6937-4}}</ref> Hillenburg compromised by creating Mrs. Puff as SpongeBob's boat-driving teacher. This satisfied Nickelodeon's request while allowing SpongeBob to remain an adult character.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Miller-Zarneke |first=Tracey |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/SpongeBob_SquarePants_The_Art_of_an_Unde/-au7EQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22having+SpongeBob+be+a+student%22&pg=PA46&printsec=frontcover |title=SpongeBob SquarePants: The Art of an Undersea World |date=2026-03-03 |publisher=IDW Publishing |language=en |isbn=979-8-88724-441-9}}</ref> According to Nickelodeon's ''SpongeBob BingePants'' podcast, Mrs. Puff's addition "saved the show" and caused Nickelodeon to agree to produce the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://podcasts.apple.com/mx/podcast/voicing-mrs-puff-with-mary-jo-catlett/id1586201809?i=1000548459780|work=[[Apple Podcasts]]|publisher=[[Paramount Skydance]]|title=Voicing Mrs. Puff with Mary Jo Catlett - ''SpongeBob BingePants''|date=January 20, 2022}}</ref>

Beginning with the [[SpongeBob SquarePants season 11|eleventh season]], the series' writers began an effort to give more storylines to the four main female characters (Karen, Sandy, Mrs. Puff, and Pearl).<ref name="peoplemag">{{cite news|url=https://people.com/spongebob-squarepants-female-cast-opens-up-about-25-year-sisterhood-11699789|title=''SpongeBob SquarePants'' Female Voice Cast Says They're 'More Like Sisters' After 25 Years of Working Together|work=[[People (magazine)|People]]|date=March 20, 2025|last=Andaloro|first=Angela}}</ref> This led to the creation of the "Gal Pals," a friend group between the female characters, first introduced in the episode "Girls' Night Out."<ref name="peoplemag"/> In an interview with ''[[People (magazine)|People]]'', Lori Alan explained, "Little by little, we've really been able to have more female plotlines."<ref name="peoplemag"/> Jill Talley added, "It's nice too for all the little girls out there to see representation on the show."<ref name="peoplemag"/>

===SpongeBob SquarePants===
{{main|SpongeBob SquarePants (character)}}

SpongeBob SquarePants (voiced by [[Tom Kenny]])<!-- Voiced by Tom Kenny in almost all media, so no need to list one-time voices here --> is an anthropomorphic and energetic yellow [[Aplysina fistularis|sea sponge]] who usually wears brown short pants, a white collared shirt, and a red tie. Like real sea sponges, he can [[filter feeding|filter-feed]] and reproduce by [[budding]].<ref>{{cite episode|title=[[Pressure (SpongeBob SquarePants)|Pressure]]|series=SpongeBob SquarePants}}</ref> He lives in a [[pineapple]] house and is employed as a fry cook at a fast food restaurant called the [[Krusty Krab]].<ref name="meet">{{cite web|url=http://www.nick-asia.com/sites/spongebob/main.html|title=SpongeBob SquarePants: Meet Your Sea Friends|work=[[Nickelodeon (Southeast Asia)|Nickelodeon Southeast Asia]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100622041552/http://www.nick-asia.com/sites/spongebob/main.html|archive-date=June 22, 2010}}</ref> He diligently attends Mrs. Puff's Boating School but has never passed the test; throughout the series, he tries his hardest on the exams, but remains an unintentionally reckless boat driver and often causes accidents. He is relentlessly optimistic and enthusiastic toward his job and his friends. SpongeBob's hobbies include catching [[jellyfish]], blowing bubbles, playing with his best friend Patrick, and unintentionally irritating his bad-tempered neighbor Squidward. He first appears in "[[Help Wanted (SpongeBob SquarePants)|Help Wanted]]".<ref name="Neuwirth, p. 51" />

===Patrick Star===
{{main|Patrick Star}}

Patrick Star (voiced by [[Bill Fagerbakke]])<!-- Voiced by Bill Fagerbakke in almost all media, so no need to list one-time voices here --> is a pink [[starfish]] who lives under a rock and wears green and purple flowered swim trunks. His most prominent character trait is his extremely low intelligence. He is best friends with SpongeBob and often unknowingly encourages activities that could get the two into lots of trouble.<ref name="meet" /> While typically unemployed throughout the series, Patrick holds various short-term jobs as the storyline of each episode requires, particularly with various stints at the Krusty Krab. He is generally slow and even-tempered, but can sometimes get very aggressive, much like real starfish, and occasionally performs feats of great strength.<ref>{{cite news|author=Hutchins, Jeff|year=2010|title=The Oral History of ''SpongeBob SquarePants''|work=[[Hogan's Alley (magazine)|Hogan's Alley]] #17|publisher=Bull Moose Publishing Corporation|url=http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/|url-status=dead|access-date=September 21, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831044034/http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/|archive-date=August 31, 2015}}</ref>

===Squidward Tentacles===
{{main|Squidward Tentacles}}

Squidward Tentacles (voiced by [[Rodger Bumpass]])<!-- Voiced by Rodger Bumpass in almost all media, so no need to list one-time voices here --> is a [[Turquoise (color)|turquoise]] bad-tempered [[Giant Pacific octopus]]<!--Please DO NOT replace with "squid". Squidward is officially confirmed as a Giant Pacific octopus and is not a squid.--> with a large nose who works as a cashier at the Krusty Krab, but despises his job and desires a much better life. He is SpongeBob's next-door neighbor with a dry, sarcastic sense of humor. His house is between SpongeBob's and Patrick's houses.<ref>{{cite web|last=Reardon|first=Samantha|date=September 8, 2013|title=Rodger Bumpass is Squidward Tentacles|url=http://georgiastatesignal.com/rodger-bumpass-is-squidward-tentacles/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328111302/http://georgiastatesignal.com/rodger-bumpass-is-squidward-tentacles/|archive-date=March 28, 2014|access-date=March 28, 2014|work=[[The Signal (college newspaper)|The Signal]]}}</ref> He believes himself to be a talented artist and musician, but nobody else recognizes his abilities. He plays the [[clarinet]] and often paints self-portraits in different styles, which he hangs up around his [[moai]] house. Squidward frequently voices his great frustration with SpongeBob, but he genuinely cares for him deep down and will occasionally stick up for him. This has been revealed in the form of sudden confessions when Squidward is in a dire situation or when SpongeBob is severely treated unfairly.

===Mr. Krabs===
{{main|Mr. Krabs}}

Eugene Krabs (voiced by [[Clancy Brown]]) is a red [[crab]] who lives in an [[anchor]]-shaped house with his daughter Pearl, who is a [[whale]]. He dislikes spending money but will go to great lengths to make Pearl very happy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nickelodeonuniverse.com/character/mr-krabs/|title=Mr. Krabs at Nickelodeon Universe|work=[[Mall of America]]|publisher=[[Triple Five Group]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606093935/https://nickelodeonuniverse.com/character/mr-krabs/|archive-date=June 6, 2017}}</ref> Mr. Krabs owns and operates the Krusty Krab restaurant where SpongeBob and Squidward work. He is self-content, cunning, and very obsessed with the value and essence of money.<ref name="meet"/> He tends to worry much more about his riches than about the needs of his employees. Having served in the navy, he speaks like a stereotypical pirate and loves sailing, whales and [[sea shanty|sea shanties]].

===Plankton and Karen===
{{main|Plankton and Karen}}

Sheldon Plankton (voiced by [[Mr. Lawrence]]) and Karen Plankton (voiced by [[Jill Talley]]) are the owners of the Chum Bucket, an unsuccessful restaurant located across the street from the Krusty Krab. Their business is a commercial failure because they sell mostly inedible foods made from [[chumming|chum]]. Plankton is a small dark green [[plankton]]ic [[copepod]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-82792771.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610060614/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-82792771.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=June 10, 2014|title=Stephen Hillenburg created the undersea world of SpongeBob|date=February 12, 2002|newspaper=[[Orange County Register]]|last=Wilson|first=Amy|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and the self-proclaimed archenemy of Mr. Krabs. His ultimate goal is to steal Krabs' secret formula for Krabby Patties, run the Krusty Krab out of business, and take over the world, but he never permanently succeeds, usually due to either SpongeBob and/or Krabs' efforts, his own incompetence and immaturity, or his own small size (except, temporarily, in ''[[The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie]]''). Plankton is a skilled inventor and possesses a [[Napoleon complex]] due to his short stature.<ref name="Absorbing">{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lT7VzFW0acE |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211219/lT7VzFW0acE |archive-date=2021-12-19 |url-status=live|title=The Absorbing Tale Behind "The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie"|last=Lawrence|first=Doug|author-link=Mr. Lawrence|date=March 1, 2005|time=9:50–9:58|quote=Plankton's about this big, a little cyclops ... he's got a little bit of a Napoleon complex, I'd say.}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Karen is Plankton's own invention, a waterproof supercomputer<ref name="characterguide">{{cite web|title=''SpongeBob SquarePants'' Character Guide Refresh|url=https://issuu.com/dhosford/docs/sb_character_guide|date=July 22, 2016|page=3|work=Nickelodeon Consumer Products|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|quote=Nowhere else could you expect to find a cast that includes a scuba-diving squirrel, Sandy Cheeks, and a waterproof supercomputer, Karen.|access-date=February 28, 2019|archive-date=August 7, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807141336/https://issuu.com/dhosford/docs/sb_character_guide|url-status=dead}}</ref> who is more competent than Plankton, being the brains behind most of his evil plans to steal Krabs' secret recipe.<ref name="nz">{{cite web|url=http://www.nicknz.co.nz/shows/SpongeBob%20SquarePants/show.html|title=Characters of ''SpongeBob SquarePants''|work=[[Nickelodeon (New Zealand)|Nickelodeon New Zealand]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071010072941/http://www.nicknz.co.nz/shows/SpongeBob%20SquarePants/show.html|archive-date=October 10, 2007}}</ref> She is married to Plankton and usually takes residence in the Chum Bucket laboratory. Karen speaks with a pronounced [[North-Central American English|Midwestern American]] accent.

===Sandy Cheeks===
{{main|Sandy Cheeks}}

Sandy Cheeks (voiced by [[Carolyn Lawrence]])<!-- Voiced by Carolyn Lawrence in almost all media, so no need to list one-time voices here --> is a brown squirrel from [[Texas]] who lives in an air-filled glass dome and wears a diving suit to be able to breathe underwater.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sandy – Nickelodeon Sweden|url=http://nickelodeon.se/nick/whats_on/characters/characterDetail.jhtml?articleId=30049880|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051018105124/http://nickelodeon.se/nick/whats_on/characters/characterDetail.jhtml;jsessionid=W3MG1WGZDUDW3QFIAIISFE4AVABBEIV0?articleId=30049880|archive-date=October 18, 2005|work=[[Viacom International Media Networks Europe|MTV Networks Europe]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]}}</ref> When aquatic creatures enter her home, they wear helmets of water to survive.<ref name="meet-the-gang">{{cite web|title=''SpongeBob SquarePants'': Meet the Gang!|url=http://www.nickelodeon.com.au/fullynick/tvshows/shows/spongebob-squarepants-show|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080310224329/http://www.nickelodeon.com.au/fullynick/tvshows/shows/spongebob-squarepants-show|archive-date=March 10, 2008|work=[[Nickelodeon (Australia and New Zealand)]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]}}</ref> Sandy speaks with a [[Southern American English|Southern]] drawl and often uses Texas slang. Her hobbies include extreme sports, science experiments, and karate. Sandy is also a member of the Gal Pals, a friend group with Karen, Mrs. Puff, and Pearl.<ref>{{cite web | title=The SpongeBob "Gal Pals" Reflected on Their Incredible 25-Year Friendship | website=[[BuzzFeed]] | date=March 18, 2025 | url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/andrewfirriolo/spongebob-cast-gal-pals-interview }}</ref>

===Mrs. Puff===
{{main|Mrs. Puff}}

Mrs. Puff<!--Don't include her first name, as that is in-universe format.--> (voiced by [[Mary Jo Catlett]]) is a paranoid [[pufferfish]] who is SpongeBob's teacher at boating school, an underwater driver's education facility where students drive boats like cars. She wears a sailor suit and her school is a lighthouse. SpongeBob is Mrs. Puff's most dedicated student and knows the answer to every question on her written and oral exams, but always panics and crashes when he actually tries to drive.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nicksplat.com/Tvshows/Characters/Nicktoons/Spongebob_squarepants/mrs_puff.html|title=NickSplat: Mrs. Puff Biography|work=[[Nickelodeon]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081103070725/http://www.nicksplat.com/Tvshows/Characters/Nicktoons/Spongebob_squarepants/mrs_puff.html|url-status=unfit|archive-date=November 3, 2008}}</ref> She puffs up into a ball when she is scared or injured.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nickelodeonuniverse.com/character/mrs-puff/|title=Mrs. Puff at Nickelodeon Universe|work=[[Mall of America]]|publisher=[[Triple Five Group]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606214926/http://nickelodeonuniverse.com/character/mrs-puff/|archive-date=June 6, 2017}}</ref> As a [[running gag]], she is frequently [[arrested]] by the police, usually due to her being responsible for SpongeBob when he unintentionally causes destruction around Bikini Bottom during his boating tests.

===Pearl Krabs===
{{main|Pearl Krabs}}

Pearl Krabs (voiced by [[Lori Alan]]) is a teenage [[sperm whale]]<ref>{{cite news|last=Gold|first=Michael|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/02/arts/spongebob-tony-nominations.html|title=Before the Tonys, SpongeBob Seized the Culture With Memes|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=May 2, 2018|access-date=May 3, 2018|quote=The principal characters in 'SpongeBob SquarePants' are ... a teenage sperm whale who is somehow the crab’s daughter}}</ref> and Mr. Krabs' daughter.<ref name="nz"/> She wants to fit in with her fish peers, but finds this impossible to do because of the large size inherent to her species. She will inherit the Krusty Krab from her father when she grows older, but is still in high school and does not yet have a job at the family business. Pearl's favorite activities are working at the Bikini Bottom Mall, using her father's credit card to buy anything that is in style, and listening to [[pop music]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nickelodeon.dk/nick/whats_on/characters/characterDetail.jhtml?articleId=30050383|title=Pearl – Nickelodeon Denmark|work=[[Viacom International Media Networks Europe|MTV Networks Europe]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051020034041/http://www.nickelodeon.dk/nick/whats_on/characters/characterDetail.jhtml;jsessionid=DQNYCUK20401XQFIAIICFE4AVABBCIV0?articleId=30050383|archive-date=October 20, 2005}}</ref>

===Gary the Snail===
Gary the Snail (vocal effects provided by [[Tom Kenny]]) is SpongeBob's pet [[sea snail]] who lives with him in their pineapple home and [[Meow|vocalizes like a cat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nicksplat.com/Tvshows/Characters/Nicktoons/Spongebob_squarepants/gary.html|title=NickSplat: Gary Biography|work=[[Nickelodeon]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090801153438/http://www.nicksplat.com/Tvshows/Characters/Nicktoons/Spongebob_squarepants/gary.html|url-status=unfit|archive-date=August 1, 2009}}</ref> Other snails and SpongeBob can understand and talk to him. Depicted as a level-headed, wise, and sophisticated character, Gary often serves as a voice of reason and a [[Foil (fiction)|foil]] to SpongeBob and helps solve problems that his owner cannot solve by himself. He has a pink shell that [[Hammerspace|is impossibly spacious on the inside]].

===Patchy the Pirate===
Patchy the Pirate (portrayed by [[Tom Kenny]] in live-action and voiced by him in animated form) is the host of the series' special episodes. He is a live-action [[pirate]] and the president of the fictional ''SpongeBob'' fan club. He lives in an unnamed suburb of [[Encino, Los Angeles]], [[California]], and segments hosted by him are often presented in a [[dual narrative]] with the animated stories.

Patchy has interacted with SpongeBob in "SpongeBob's Big Birthday Blowout" where he sent his head to SpongeBob as a gift.

In "SpongeBob's Road to Christmas", Patchy was seen in animated form when SpongeBob, Patrick, and Plankton stumbled upon his Christmas theme park side hustle that had him operating as [[Santa Claus]]. He does provide them with a map to the [[North Pole]].

Patchy made a special guest star appearance on ''[[Big Time Rush (TV series)|Big Time Rush]]'' in the episode "[[Big Time Beach Party]]", where he interacted with [[Carlos PenaVega|Carlos Pena Jr.]] and [[Logan Henderson]].

====Potty the Parrot====
Potty the Parrot (voiced by [[Stephen Hillenburg]] in seasons 2–3, [[Paul Tibbitt]] from seasons 5–8, [[Mr. Lawrence]] from seasons 10–present) is Patchy's green pet parrot, depicted as a crudely made puppet with [[googly eyes]]. The character's name is a reference to "Polly wants a cracker," a phrase often used for parrots to [[talking bird|vocally mimic]]. Potty is quite obnoxious and often annoys or talks back to Patchy while he is trying to host an episode.

===French Narrator===
The French Narrator (voiced by [[Tom Kenny]], portrayed by [[Dan Southworth]] and [[Vincent Waller]] in live-action appearances)<ref>{{cite tweet|user=VincentWaller72|first=Vincent|last=Waller|number=1281683682726522880|date=11 July 2020|title=Dan Southworth, he was also Frenchy wearing the suit in the water on the Feral Friends episode.}}</ref> is an [[oceanographer]] who films SpongeBob's world using a camera. He often introduces episodes from off-screen or narrates the [[intertitle]]s as if the series were a nature documentary about the ocean. He has a thick [[French language|French]] accent as a reference to the distinctive speaking style of oceanographer and filmmaker [[Jacques Cousteau]]. He is normally only heard, but physically appears three times. In "No Free Rides", after being accidentally hit by SpongeBob during a driving test, his legs, which are wearing [[scuba diving]] fins, are visible.

In "Feral Friends" and "SpongeBob's Big Birthday Blowout", he is shown in live action as a [[Standard diving dress|hard hat diver]] with his face obscured by his helmet and a red [[Beanie (seamed cap)|beanie hat]] on top, referencing the beanie hat Cousteau was widely known for wearing. In "Mimic Madness", SpongeBob impersonates him by imitating his voice and wearing a beanie and beard, once again referencing Cousteau.

Mermaid Man (voiced by [[Ernest Borgnine]] as an old man and a young man in "The Bad Guy Club for Villains", [[Adam West]] as a young man in "Back to the Past") and his sidekick Barnacle Boy (voiced by [[Tim Conway]] as an old man and a young man in "The Bad Guy Club for Villains", [[Burt Ward]] as a young man in "Back to the Past")<ref name=actors>{{cite news |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/ae/20020702spongebob0702p3.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040822045639/http://www.post-gazette.com/ae/20020702spongebob0702p3.asp |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 22, 2004 |title='SpongeBob SquarePants' is soaking up viewers |author=L. A. Johnson |date=July 2, 2002 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |access-date=2009-02-07}}</ref> are two elderly, semi-retired [[superhero]]es who live in Shady Shoals, a retirement home, and are stars of SpongeBob and Patrick's favorite television show. Mermaid Man is a stereotypically [[Senility|senile]] senior citizen who dramatically yells "Evil!" whenever he hears the word, while Barnacle Boy is shown to be the smarter, more sensible, and more irritable of the two. [[Aquaman]] artist [[Ramona Fradon]] drew the characters' comic book adventures.<ref>{{cite book|title= Superheroes!: Capes, cowls, and the creation of comic book culture|first1=Laurence|last1=Maslon|author-link1=Laurence Maslon|first2=Michael|last2=Kantor|page=167}}</ref> A series of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' official collectors' trading cards published by [[Topps]] gives their last names as Huckler and Strangler.

Since Borgnine and Conway's deaths in 2012 and 2019, respectively, both characters have been limited to [[cameo appearance]]s without dialogue, as the showrunners chose not to recast their voices.

===The Flying Dutchman===
The Flying Dutchman (voiced by [[Brian Doyle-Murray]] in the TV series, [[Mark Hamill]] in ''[[The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants]]'') is an irritable, mischievous pirate ghost who glows green.<ref name="sidecharacters">{{cite web|url=http://www.nick.com/spongebob-squarepants/games/spongebob-squarepants-which-spongebob-side-character-are-you/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170217054306/http://www.nick.com/spongebob-squarepants/games/spongebob-squarepants-which-spongebob-side-character-are-you/|url-status=dead|archive-date=2017-02-17|title=Which ''SpongeBob'' Side Character Are You?|work=[[Nick.com]]|publisher=[[Viacom International]]}}</ref> He is named after the ghost ship [[Flying Dutchman|of the same name]]. He haunts the seven seas because his unburied corpse was used as a window display. He collects souls as a [[Satan]]-like character and resides in a cavern containing [[Davy Jones' Locker]], a literal [[locker]] stuffed with very smelly socks that belong to [[The Monkees|Monkees]] singer [[Davy Jones (musician)|Davy Jones]], which within the series is analogous to [[Hell]] and occasionally mentioned as a [[curse word]].

===King Neptune===
King Neptune (voiced by [[John O'Hurley]] in the TV series, [[Paul Tibbitt]] in "SpongeBob vs. The Patty Gadget") is a very powerful, [[trident]]-wielding [[merman]] god who rules the sea, based on the [[Roman mythology|Roman mythological]] deity [[Neptune (mythology)|of the same name]]. In the series, Neptune lives in a palace in [[Atlantis]] with his wife [[Amphitrite]] and son [[Triton (mythology)|Triton]]. He is usually portrayed as very arrogant and selfish, showing little sympathy for the sea's fish populace. Neptune has a mostly teal color scheme with a long auburn beard and hair. He wears gold wrist bands and a matching crown decorated with a scallop ornament, plus a gold belt bearing a [[seahorse]] emblem. This version was also known as Neptune XIV as seen when his portrait is shown in Squidward's briefly redecorated room as seen in "Krusty Towers".

A different King Neptune is featured in ''[[The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie]]'', voiced by [[Jeffrey Tambor]]. In the film, he resides near Bikini Bottom with his daughter Mindy and resembles a light green-skinned king with a robe, a shorter beard and hair, a domed crown to cover his bald spot, and powers limited to what can be exercised through his trident.

In ''The Patrick Star Show'' episode "Neptune's Ball", the King Neptune seen in the main series holds the titular ball that the Star family thought they were invited to when Patrick got a hold of Lady Upturn's invitation to it. When King Neptune arrives after the Star family was caught by the guards trespassing, King Neptune recognizes Patrick and has them released since he is a big fan of Patrick's show. Through Patrick's suggestion, King Neptune moves the party to the Star family's house.

They are proud of SpongeBob, but embarrassed that he still does not have a driver's license.

====Ancestors====
* '''{{visible anchor|Primitive Sponge|Primitive Star}}''' and '''Primitive Star''' (voiced by [[Tom Kenny]] and [[Bill Fagerbakke]]) are the earliest known ancestors of SpongeBob and Patrick, who appear in the episode "SB-129" when Squidward time-travels to the past. Upon seeing the two of them electrocuting themselves with a jellyfish, Squidward inadvertently teaches them the sport of Jellyfishing, which results in Squidward being documented as the inventor of Jellyfishing when he returns to the present. They also seem to strongly dislike Squidward's clarinet music, as they ruthlessly chase down Squidward upon hearing it. The scene where Primitive Sponge and Primitive Star are confronted by Squidward upon noticing them torturing themselves with the jellyfish, particularly, the pose struck by Primitive Sponge, has become an [[internet meme]], referred to as "SpongeGar" (which was actually the name given to another of SpongeBob's primitive ancestors in the episode "Ugh").
* '''{{visible anchor|SpongeGar|Patar|Squog|Primitive Gary|Primitive Krabs}}''', '''Patar''', and '''Squog''' (voiced by [[Tom Kenny]], [[Bill Fagerbakke]], and [[Rodger Bumpass]]) are SpongeBob, Patrick, and Squidward's neolithic ancestors who appear in "Ugh." While still not being able to speak intelligibly, they are more advanced than the primitive ancestors in "SB-129" as they are shown to use stone tools and fire. Also appearing in the episode are '''Primitive Gary''' (voiced by Tom Kenny), Gary's gigantic ancestor and SpongeGar's pet, and '''Primitive Krabs''' (voiced by [[Clancy Brown]]), Mr. Krabs' tiny ancestor who repeatedly chants "money."
* '''{{visible anchor|SpongeTron|Patron}}''' and '''Patron''' (voiced by [[Tom Kenny]] and [[Bill Fagerbakke]]) are SpongeBob and Patrick's robotic descendants who appear in "SB-129". SpongeTron has 486 clones, each one named after a letter of the English alphabet from 2,000 years in the future, while Patron has two heads.

==Reception==
{{See also|List of awards and nominations received by SpongeBob SquarePants{{!}}List of awards and nominations received by ''SpongeBob SquarePants''}}
The characters of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' have been well-received overall. The titular character SpongeBob has become very popular with children and adults.
The character's popularity has spread from Nickelodeon's original demographic of two- to eleven-year-olds, to teenagers and adults.<ref name=foxgay>{{cite news |url=https://www.foxnews.com/story/spongebob-hotpants|title=SpongeBob HotPants?|last=Park|first=Michael Y.|date=2002-10-09|publisher=[[Fox News Channel]]|access-date=2008-11-09}}</ref><ref name=goodlife>{{cite news |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/money/covers/2002-05-17-sponge-bob.htm |title=Life's good for SpongeBob |first=Gary |last=Strauss |date=May 17, 2002 |newspaper=[[USA Today]]|access-date=2016-09-25}}</ref> The popularity of SpongeBob translated well into sales figures. In 2002, SpongeBob SquarePants dolls sold at a rate of 75,000 per week, which was faster than [[Tickle Me Elmo]] dolls were selling at the time.<ref name=goodlife /> SpongeBob has gained popularity in Japan, specifically with Japanese women. Nickelodeon's parent company [[Viacom (2005–present)|Viacom]] purposefully targeted marketing at women in the country as a method of building the ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' brand. Skeptics initially doubted that SpongeBob could be popular in Japan as the character's design is very different from already popular designs for [[Hello Kitty]] and [[Pikachu]].<ref name="SFGate">{{cite news|url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/n/a/2007/01/24/entertainment/e091755S47.DTL |title=SpongeBob Goes Trendy to Win Japan Fans |last=Kageyama |first=Yuri |date=2007-01-24 |newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |access-date=2008-11-08 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219071843/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fn%2Fa%2F2007%2F01%2F24%2Fentertainment%2Fe091755S47.DTL |archive-date=December 19, 2008 }}</ref> However, the characters have also attracted some negative reception, including SpongeBob himself, who was listed as number four on AskMen's ''Top 10: Irritating '90s Cartoon Characters''. Nevertheless, SpongeBob SquarePants was ranked ninth on ''TV Guide'''s top 50 cartoon characters.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.askmen.com/top_10/entertainment_200/234b_top_10_list.html|title=Top 10: Irritating '90s Cartoon Characters|last=Murphy|first=Ryan|publisher=[[AskMen]]|access-date=2008-11-08|archive-date=March 19, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319153425/http://www.askmen.com/top_10/entertainment_200/234b_top_10_list.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Appearances in other media==
{{See also|SpongeBob SquarePants (film series){{!}}''SpongeBob SquarePants'' (film series)|List of SpongeBob SquarePants merchandise{{!}}List of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' merchandise}}
The characters of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' appeared in the 2004 theatrical film ''[[The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie]]'' and its [[The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water|2015 sequel]]. Both films feature the regular television cast and blend animated elements with live-action sequences. They have also been featured in a variety of associated [[List of SpongeBob SquarePants merchandise|merchandise]], particularly video games; from 2001 to 2013, the ''SpongeBob'' franchise had multiple video games released each year, with the show's voice cast reprising their character roles for many titles.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nickelodeon to ramp up console offering, starting with ''The Loud House''|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-10-12-nickelodeon-to-ramp-up-console-offering-starting-with-the-loud-house|work=GamesIndustry|publisher=[[Eurogamer]]|last=Batchelor|first=James|date=October 12, 2017|access-date=November 12, 2017}}</ref> Every main cast member with the exception of [[Clancy Brown]] has voiced their respective characters in each game that they appear; Brown's character [[Mr. Krabs]] is instead voiced by [[Joe Whyte]] in ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants: SuperSponge|SuperSponge]]'', ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants: Operation Krabby Patty|Operation Krabby Patty]]'', and ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom|Battle for Bikini Bottom]]'' and by [[Bob Joles]] in the [[SpongeBob's Truth or Square (video game)|''Truth or Square'' game]].

The ''SpongeBob'' characters have been featured at a variety of theme park attractions. In 2003, [[Kings Island]] announced plans to build the first ''SpongeBob''-themed amusement park ride, a [[dark ride]] roller coaster titled "Mrs. Puff's Crash Course Boating School".<ref>{{cite web|title=Paramount Parks Development Survey|url=http://www.parkfeedback.com:80/research/survey.aspx?s=CONC2004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040911224249/http://www.parkfeedback.com/research/survey.aspx?s=CONC2004|archive-date=September 11, 2004|publisher=[[Viacom International]]|work=[[Paramount Parks]]|access-date=9 October 2010|date=September 8, 2004|last=Kupferman|first=Mark|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Plans were halted when Kings Island changed ownership, and the first ride featuring ''SpongeBob'' theming was instead "SpongeBob's Boatmobiles"—also based on Mrs. Puff's Boating School and opened in 2003—at [[California's Great America]].<ref name="UltimateRC GA opening">{{cite web|title=Ten New Nickelodeon Rides and Attractions For Paramount's Great America|url=http://www.ultimaterollercoaster.com/news/archives/2003/stories/031203_01.shtml|work=Press Release|publisher=Ultimate Rollercoaster|access-date=9 October 2010|date=12 March 2003}}</ref> Amusement rides based on the characters have since been opened at [[Blackpool Pleasure Beach]], [[Dreamworld (Australian theme park)|Dreamworld]], [[Movie Park Germany]], and [[Nickelodeon Universe]]. Two [[4D film]]s featuring 3-D models of the characters and a [[motion simulator]] experience, ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants 4-D]]'' and ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants 4D: The Great Jelly Rescue|The Great Jelly Rescue]]'', were sold to theme parks and aquariums worldwide in 2005 and 2013 respectively.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brand-New Entertainment Experiences with ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' and ''Dora the Explorer'' Only at the Nick Hotel in Orlando |url=http://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20130424005204/en/Celebrate-Brand-New-Entertainment-Experiences-SpongeBob-SquarePants-Dora |work=[[Business Wire]] |publisher=[[Berkshire Hathaway]] |date=April 24, 2013}}</ref>

Mascot costumes of the ''SpongeBob'' characters debuted at [[Holiday Inn Resort Orlando Suites – Waterpark|Nickelodeon Suites Resort]] in 2005 and have made regular appearances at Nickelodeon events since.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nickhotel.com/entertainment/characters|title=Nickelodeon Suites Resort Character Appearances|work=[[Nickelodeon Suites Resort]]|url-status=unfit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140614074214/http://www.nickhotel.com/entertainment/characters|archive-date=June 14, 2014}}</ref> Plankton, Karen, and Gary are the only main characters who have never been realized as mascots;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.awn.com/news/spongebob-fan-shellabration-headed-universal-studios|title=SpongeBob Fan 'Shellabration' Headed to Universal Studios|work=[[Animation World Network]]|date=August 29, 2013|last=Wolfe|first=Jennifer}}</ref> at events, they are normally depicted as puppets or statues instead. In December 2011, a parade of ''SpongeBob'' mascots and floats titled "SpongeBob ParadePants" opened at [[Sea World (Australia)|Sea World Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://themeparks.com.au/~/media/Files/Shared/domestic%20sales/sw1205603_Trade_Brochure.ashx#page=2|title=Gold Coast Theme Parks Trade Brochure 2012|work=Gold Coast Attractions|url-status=unfit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121011175137/http://themeparks.com.au/~/media/Files/Shared/domestic%20sales/sw1205603_Trade_Brochure.ashx|archive-date=October 11, 2012}}</ref> In November 2017, a [[SpongeBob SquarePants (musical)|Broadway musical]] based on the show began previews at the [[Palace Theatre (New York City)|Palace Theatre]], and opened in December 2017. Unlike previous shows, the characters were not represented with mascot costumes but by actors wearing clothing inspired by the characters' designs.

===Popular culture===
The characters of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' have appeared throughout popular culture. In 2007, the [[Amsterdam]]-based company [[Boom Chicago]] created a ''SpongeBob'' [[parody]] called "SpongeBob SquarePants in China", in which a stereotypically Chinese Patrick refuses to go to work and advocates [[freedom of speech]], rights of leisure, and income.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.boomchicago.tv/boomvideosearch/node |title=Official Boom Chicago "Back to Work!" page |publisher=Boomchicago.tv |access-date=2011-08-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110911011157/http://www.boomchicago.tv/boomvideosearch/node |archive-date=September 11, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> During the same year, production company [[Camp Chaos]] created a ''SpongeBob'' parody titled ''SpongeBong HempPants'', which features five of the series' characters parodied in the form of various [[drugs]]. The show was seen on [[VH1]] and [[Comedy Central]], both owned by Nickelodeon's parent company Viacom.<ref name="TV Squad">{{cite web |url=http://www.tvsquad.com/2007/01/01/spongebong-the-banned/ |title=SpongeBong the banned |access-date=2009-11-13 |author=Finley, Adam |date=2007-01-01|publisher=TV Squad|archive-date=October 28, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081028083504/http://www.tvsquad.com/2007/01/01/spongebong-the-banned/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Comedy Central's ''[[Drawn Together]]'' also features a parody of SpongeBob named "Wooldoor Sockbat" whose theme tune is inspired by ''SpongeBob''{{'}}s Hawaiian-style background music. Two animated series that former ''SpongeBob'' writer [[Dan Povenmire]] worked on have incorporated references to the characters; the ''[[Phineas and Ferb]]'' special "[[Phineas and Ferb: Summer Belongs To You!|Summer Belongs to You]]" features a joke in which [[Phineas Flynn]] holds up inanimate representations of SpongeBob and Patrick, and the ''[[Family Guy]]'' episode "[[Road to Rupert]]" includes SpongeBob's "Campfire Song Song" from "[[SpongeBob SquarePants season 3#ep57b|The Camping Episode]]". SpongeBob, Patrick, Mr. Krabs, Pearl and Squidward all appear in "[[Robot Chicken season 5##ep87|Major League of Extraordinary Gentlemen]]", an episode of the sketch comedy ''[[Robot Chicken]]''. A segment of the episode, animated in [[stop motion]] with ''SpongeBob'' toy figures, features Mr. Krabs using crab legs as the secret ingredient for Krabby Patties.<ref>{{cite episode|title=Major League of Extraordinary Gentlemen |series=[[Robot Chicken]] |season=5 |number=87 |network=[[Adult Swim]] |airdate=February 13, 2011 |credits=Writers: [[Mike Fasolo]], [[Seth Green]], [[Matthew Senreich]], [[Zeb Wells]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ggb-_zU3yz4 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221232850/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ggb-_zU3yz4 |archive-date=February 21, 2015 }}</ref> In April 2016, [[Nintendo]]'s [[Wii U]] exclusive ''[[Splatoon]]'' released a splatfest based on the eponymous series by teaming two characters [[SpongeBob SquarePants (character)|SpongeBob]] and [[Patrick Star|Patrick]], hosted by the pop band [[Squid Sisters]]: Callie and Marie, the event began for 24 hours and Team Patrick won.
